intro: 50 ADHD topics with a strong chance of spreading on LinkedIn: specific, relatable, slightly contrarian, and easy to tell as a story. A fresh set is written on the 1st of every month, and no hook from a previous month is reused.
note: First-person prompts assume lived experience. If it isn't yours, frame it as what you've heard from users (with permission), or pick another prompt. No medical claims and no invented numbers: fill [placeholders] with real ones.

prompts.hook: I didn't miss the deadline because I didn't care. I missed it because I cared too much to start.
prompts.prompt: Write about the gap between caring and starting at work, and the one thing that finally closes it for you.

prompts.hook: A 30-minute meeting costs my ADHD brain the whole afternoon.
prompts.prompt: Explain the hidden cost of context-switching, then propose one meeting norm every team could adopt this week.

prompts.hook: My best performance review came from my worst habit.
prompts.prompt: Tell the story of hyperfocus as both an asset and a liability, and what you now do to steer it.

prompts.hook: What I wish my first manager knew about ADHD.
prompts.prompt: Five short, specific things a manager could do differently, one per slide. Make them practical, not a lecture.

prompts.hook: Open-plan offices are an accessibility issue.
prompts.prompt: Make a respectful contrarian case, with one concrete alternative that works for everyone.

prompts.hook: Job interviews test performance under pressure, not the work itself.
prompts.prompt: Write about interviewing with ADHD and suggest one change hiring teams could make tomorrow.

prompts.hook: Should you tell your employer you have ADHD?
prompts.prompt: Share the honest trade-offs from your own experience or from people you've spoken to. Don't give legal advice; describe what helped and what didn't.

prompts.hook: The ADHD tax at work that nobody budgets for.
prompts.prompt: List the real costs: missed reimbursements, forgotten renewals, late fees. Use your own [examples] and end with one fix for each.

prompts.hook: Remote work saved my career, and nearly ended it.
prompts.prompt: Write both sides: what home working unlocks for ADHD brains and what it quietly takes away.

prompts.hook: 3 tiny changes that help your ADHD teammates (and everyone else).
prompts.prompt: Written agendas, one named owner per task, async updates. Explain why each one works, in a sentence.

prompts.hook: ADHD isn't a lack of attention. It's a lack of control over where attention goes.
prompts.prompt: Unpack the reframe with one everyday example that makes it click for people without ADHD.

prompts.hook: “Just make a to-do list” is the “just calm down” of productivity advice.
prompts.prompt: Explain why generic advice backfires, and what actually helps instead.

prompts.hook: “Lazy” is a story people tell about a wall they can't see.
prompts.prompt: Describe task paralysis from the inside, kindly and specifically, without self-pity.

prompts.hook: “Everyone's a little ADHD.” Here's why that line stings.
prompts.prompt: Explain how casual phrases minimize a real struggle. Be warm, not preachy, and offer a better thing to say.

prompts.hook: Hyperfocus isn't a superpower. It's a steering problem.
prompts.prompt: Push back on the superpower narrative with an honest story about where hyperfocus took you that you didn't choose.

prompts.hook: Discipline didn't fix it. Design did.
prompts.prompt: Show how changing your environment beat willpower: one before/after setup, with a photo.

prompts.hook: “I'll remember” is the most expensive sentence I say.
prompts.prompt: A short, funny-but-true post about everything “I'll remember” has cost you, ending with the capture habit that fixed it.

prompts.hook: Rest feels like falling behind.
prompts.prompt: Write about guilt, rest and the ADHD brain, and the permission you had to give yourself.

prompts.hook: 5 things people assume about adults with ADHD (that aren't true).
prompts.prompt: Myth on one slide, reality on the next. Keep every reality supportable and cite sources in the caption.

prompts.hook: Procrastination isn't a time problem. It's a feeling problem.
prompts.prompt: Explain the emotional side of avoidance (credit the researchers you draw on) and one way to lower the feeling, not just push through it.

prompts.hook: I was diagnosed at [age]. Here's what I grieved first.
prompts.prompt: Write about a late diagnosis: the relief, the grief and the rewriting of your own story.

prompts.hook: Masking all day is a second full-time job.
prompts.prompt: Describe what masking looks like in a normal workday, and what you no longer hide.

prompts.hook: The 3pm crash isn't about coffee.
prompts.prompt: Describe your energy curve honestly and how you now plan the day around it rather than against it.

prompts.hook: Why one “quick question?” message can wreck my morning.
prompts.prompt: Write about rejection sensitivity at work, and the small wording change that would help.

prompts.hook: Time blindness, explained with my actual calendar.
prompts.prompt: Share a redacted screenshot of planned vs. what really happened, then say what you changed.

prompts.hook: The pile of clothes on my chair has a system. Let me explain.
prompts.prompt: A light, self-aware post about the logic behind “doom piles”, with a real photo.

prompts.hook: What ADHD looks like when you're “high-performing”.
prompts.prompt: Show the cost behind the output people see: the late nights, the last-minute rescues, the recovery.

prompts.hook: “Sorry for the late reply” is half my sent folder.
prompts.prompt: Write about communication guilt, and the reply rhythm you've settled on without apologizing.

prompts.hook: Things I've stopped apologizing for.
prompts.prompt: A short list of habits you've made peace with, and the one you're still working on.

prompts.hook: A letter to my younger self, who thought they were just lazy.
prompts.prompt: Write the note you needed at 15. Keep it specific to moments, not general encouragement.

prompts.hook: My whole productivity system fits on one sticky note.
prompts.prompt: Photograph it and explain each line. Simplicity is the point.

prompts.hook: The weirdly effective trick of working next to someone.
prompts.prompt: Explain body doubling, why it works for so many ADHD brains, and how to try it today.

prompts.hook: I tried [N] productivity apps. Here's why none of them stuck.
prompts.prompt: One reason per slide, ending with what a tool would need to get right for ADHD brains.

prompts.hook: AI won't fix ADHD. But it can hold the pieces my brain drops.
prompts.prompt: An honest take on where AI genuinely helps (capture, breaking down tasks, reminders) and where it doesn't.

prompts.hook: The 2-minute start: my rule for tasks I've avoided for weeks.
prompts.prompt: Walk through the rule in 4 steps using one real task you've been dodging.

prompts.hook: Why my keys go in the same tray every single night.
prompts.prompt: Show your “launch pad” by the door and explain the thinking behind it.

prompts.hook: I use timers to make time visible, not to work faster.
prompts.prompt: Explain visual timers and time blindness, with a photo of your actual timer.

prompts.hook: Most apps are built to capture attention. That's a problem for brains like mine.
prompts.prompt: A contrarian take on the attention economy, and what humane design would look like instead.

prompts.hook: How I plan a week when I can't predict my energy.
prompts.prompt: Show your flexible weekly plan as a simple visual: must-dos, could-dos, and buffer.

prompts.hook: The most helpful focus tool I own cost nothing.
prompts.prompt: Reveal it (another person in the room, a walk, a timer) and tell the story of the day you discovered it.

prompts.hook: Why I'm building for the 380M people productivity apps forgot.
prompts.prompt: The vision post: who's underserved, what you saw that others missed, and what Dopami is trying first.

prompts.hook: A user told me “[quote]”. It changed our roadmap.
prompts.prompt: Share the quote (with permission), what you heard underneath it, and what you changed because of it.

prompts.hook: Designing for ADHD minds made our product better for everyone.
prompts.prompt: Explain the curb-cut effect with one Dopami design decision that helps every user.

prompts.hook: What designing for ADHD taught me that years of product design didn't.
prompts.prompt: Contrast lessons from leading design at Flam and Betaflux with what you're learning at Dopami.

prompts.hook: We cut a feature to make Dopami simpler.
prompts.prompt: Tell the story only if it happened: what it was, why people liked it, and why less was kinder.

prompts.hook: Building in public, week [N]: the honest numbers.
prompts.prompt: Share real progress and real misses. Screenshot one metric you're proud of and one you're not.

prompts.hook: How many questions should an ADHD app ask on day one?
prompts.prompt: Walk through your onboarding thinking and where you landed. Invite people to disagree.

prompts.hook: What investors ask me about building for ADHD, and my answers.
prompts.prompt: One question per slide, answered plainly and confidently.

prompts.hook: The ADHD community taught me more than any research method.
prompts.prompt: Credit the communities, coaches and users who shaped Dopami, and say what each one taught you.

prompts.hook: Looking for ADHD coaches, clinicians and builders who want to shape Dopami.
prompts.prompt: A clear, warm call-out post: who you need, what they'd influence, and how to reach you.
